# Preposterior check of lever-study designs

*Generated by `scripts/generators/build_lever_design_preposterior.py` (STATUS_AND_PLAN sec. 0, owner row). For each candidate study, simulated outcomes drawn from the lever table's own posterior predictive, keyed as PREREG sec. 3 keys a real contrast, and refitted with the table's model and reading rule. A design aid: it moves no shipped number and reads no engine prediction.*

Settings: 400 simulations per design and matrix setting; within-laboratory residual 0.1 dex; SIDA CV 0.1, other analytes 0.2; a cell with no keyed estimate draws mu and the laboratory-offset scale from N(0, 0.5). Matrix shift: an offset shared by every new laboratory (all cook in pea isolate), SD 0 or 0.3 dex.

Reading: a cell is one odorant x lever (x pH band, x level for categorical levers) of `lever_table.md`; 'answered' is PREREG sec. 5 (>= 3 laboratories, the 90 % interval of mu excludes zero, P(a new laboratory sees the same sign) >= 0.8). 'Map cells' are the experiment map's family x lever cells. Yeast extract has no lever class in PREREG sec. 4, so a yeast-extract factor feeds no cell until an amendment adds one.

## Does the study improve the prediction for a new kitchen? (predictive check)

*Not the 'answered' count (that counts our own three-laboratory rule). For each simulated world, the table's prediction for one new kitchen cooking in pea isolate (its effect: mu + the matrix shift + a new laboratory offset drawn with the full tau) is scored: the chance its sign is wrong, the error of its estimate against the pea-matrix mean, and its 90 % new-laboratory interval's coverage and width. 'Oracle' is the sign error of a predictor that knows the pea-matrix mean exactly (the floor set by between-laboratory scatter). 'Confident' is P(same sign in a new laboratory) >= 0.8 (the PREREG sec. 5 sign criterion). Protocol factor 0.5: the design laboratories, sharing our protocol and lot, scatter half as much as the literature's, so the fit sees less between-laboratory spread than a new kitchen has. Same 36 pots; same simulated worlds for every design (400 per setting).*
